example.name: Lucia
example.look: olive skin, long wavy brown hair, red glasses

tagline: A warm egg, a tiny dinosaur, and one brave helper who knows the way home.
lesson_or_purpose: Kindness and responsibility: caring for someone small, noticing clues, and doing the brave, helpful thing even when it means saying goodbye.
tone: Warm, playful and gently adventurous, with moments of wonder and a cozy, satisfying ending.
reading_level: Read-aloud for ages 3-5, early independent reading for ages 6-8. Short sentences, a repeated call-and-answer sound, and vivid action words.
illustration_guide: Setting moves from a cheerful suburban backyard with a hedge, garden gate and clothesline, across a wildflower meadow and a pine forest with a rushing stream, into a hidden green valley of giant ferns, mossy boulders and a misty waterfall. Palette: leafy greens, warm sunshine yellows, sky blues and soft terracotta, shifting to golden orange at sunset. Recurring elements: the cream egg with teal speckles, the small round teal dinosaur Pip with a cream belly and stubby tail, the child's red scarf, a trail of three-toed footprints, and curled fern fronds. Style: soft painterly picture-book art with rounded shapes and friendly expressions; dinosaurs are gentle and never scary.

page_outline.beat: After a stormy night, {name} steps into the backyard and finds a warm, speckled egg nestled under the hedge. {name} kneels down and feels it gently wobble.
page_outline.illustration_prompt: Morning backyard with dewy grass and a green hedge; the child kneels in wonder beside a large cream egg with teal speckles tucked among leaves, sunlight breaking through clouds.

page_outline.beat: {name} wraps the egg in a soft red scarf and keeps it cozy, humming to it all morning. The egg rocks, taps, and a tiny crack appears.
page_outline.illustration_prompt: The child sits cross-legged on the grass hugging the speckled egg wrapped in a red scarf, a small zigzag crack on top, a curious robin watching from the clothesline.

page_outline.beat: Crack! Out pops a small, round, teal dinosaur named Pip. Pip sniffs {name}, sneezes, then looks around and gives a sad, homesick peep.
page_outline.illustration_prompt: A tiny round teal dinosaur with a cream belly bursts from the eggshell, blinking at the child, who laughs with delight; shell pieces scattered on the red scarf.

page_outline.beat: {name} spots clues: a curly fern leaf stuck to the shell and big three-toed footprints leading past the garden gate. {name} decides to take Pip home.
page_outline.illustration_prompt: The child crouches, pointing at a trail of large three-toed footprints leading through an open garden gate toward a sunny hill, the little teal dinosaur peeking at a fern leaf.

page_outline.beat: {name} packs a snack bag and leads Pip across a wildflower meadow. When Pip gets tired and hungry, {name} shares a handful of berries.
page_outline.illustration_prompt: Bright meadow of wildflowers; the child sits beside the small teal dinosaur sharing berries from an open snack bag, butterflies drifting overhead, footprints continuing toward a pine forest.

page_outline.beat: A wide, rushing stream blocks the trail and Pip is afraid of the water. {name} rolls flat stones into a row and makes a stepping-stone path.
page_outline.illustration_prompt: Pine forest stream with splashing water; the child pushes a flat stone into place to finish a stepping-stone path while the little teal dinosaur waits nervously on the bank.

page_outline.beat: Deep in the forest, thick mist hides the footprints. {name} has a clever idea: {name} asks Pip to call out loudly, and from far away a big, deep call answers.
page_outline.illustration_prompt: Misty pine forest in soft blue tones; the child kneels beside the little teal dinosaur, which tips its head back to call, while the child cups a hand to listen toward a faint glow beyond the trees.

page_outline.beat: {name} and Pip climb over a mossy ridge and see a hidden valley full of giant ferns, a waterfall, and gentle dinosaurs. Pip hides, suddenly shy, and {name} gives a brave, encouraging smile.
page_outline.illustration_prompt: Wide view of a lush green valley with giant ferns, a misty waterfall and peaceful long-necked dinosaurs; the child stands on a mossy ridge with the small teal dinosaur peeking from behind the child's legs.

page_outline.beat: A big teal mother dinosaur hurries over, and Pip runs to her with happy peeps. She lowers her head to {name}, and Pip gives {name} a goodbye nuzzle and a smooth piece of speckled shell.
page_outline.illustration_prompt: A large gentle teal dinosaur bends her long neck down to the child; the little teal dinosaur nuzzles the child's hand as the child holds a speckled shell piece, ferns glowing in warm light.

page_outline.beat: At sunset {name} is back in the backyard. {name} sets the speckled shell on the windowsill and smiles, proud of helping a small friend find home.
page_outline.illustration_prompt: Golden sunset bedroom window overlooking the backyard; the child places a speckled shell piece on the windowsill, a faint silhouette of dinosaurs on a distant hill.

cover_scene: The child stands on a mossy ridge at the edge of a lush hidden valley, holding the small round teal dinosaur, both smiling, a red scarf around the child's neck. Below are giant ferns and a misty waterfall with peaceful dinosaurs in the distance. The top third of the picture is calm, open pale blue sky with soft clouds.

sample_pages.text: {name} found a scarf, soft and red. "Stay warm, little egg," {name} said. Hum, hum, hum. Wobble, wobble. Tap!
sample_pages.scene: The child sits cross-legged on the grass hugging the speckled egg wrapped in a red scarf, a tiny crack on top, a robin watching from the clothesline.

sample_pages.text: The water rushed. Whoosh! Pip backed away. "I can fix this," said {name}. One stone, two stones, three stones. Hop, hop, hop!
sample_pages.scene: Pine forest stream; the child sets the last flat stone into a stepping-stone path as the little teal dinosaur waits nervously on the bank.

h1: Personalized Dinosaur Book for Kids: Your Child and the Dinosaur Egg
meta_title: Personalized Dinosaur Book for Kids | StoryBloom
meta_description: A personalized dinosaur book where your child finds a warm egg, meets a baby dinosaur, and leads it home to a hidden valley.
promise: Your child becomes the brave, kind helper who hatches a baby dinosaur and finds the way to bring it home.
story_summary: One morning after a storm, your child discovers a warm, speckled egg hiding under the backyard hedge. With a little care and a lot of humming, it hatches into Pip, a small teal dinosaur who clearly misses its family. Following giant footprints, your child leads Pip across a meadow, over a rushing stream and through a misty forest. Along the way your child shares snacks, builds a path, and comes up with a clever plan when the trail disappears.
why_parents: Children from three to eight are fascinated by dinosaurs, and they are also learning what it means to look after someone smaller. This story puts those two things together: your child cares for a baby dinosaur, notices when it feels homesick, and chooses to help, which gives kindness a real, exciting shape.

The adventure is full of small problems your child solves: reading footprint clues, crossing a stream, finding the way in fog. Letting go of a new friend so it can be with its family is a gentle, meaningful moment that sparks good talks about caring and doing the right thing.
for_grownups: Ask your child how Pip might have felt when it woke up far from its family, and what helps them feel better when they miss someone.
Pause at the stream and the misty forest and ask, "What would you do here?" before turning the page.
After reading, go on a backyard or park clue hunt for leaves, footprints or stones, just like the trail to the valley.

faqs.question: Are the dinosaurs scary for younger children?
faqs.answer: No. Every dinosaur is drawn round, soft and friendly, and the mother dinosaur is gentle and welcoming. The biggest challenges are a splashy stream and some fog, and both are solved calmly.

faqs.question: Does the story work for a child who is not a big dinosaur fan?
faqs.answer: Yes. At its heart it is a story about caring for a little friend and helping it get home, with plenty of outdoor adventure. Many children enjoy it simply for the hatching moment and the journey.

faqs.question: Is the ending sad because Pip goes home?
faqs.answer: The goodbye is warm rather than sad. Pip is happily reunited with its mother and gives your child a piece of speckled shell to keep, and the book ends with your child feeling proud at sunset.
